立.name: Stand
立.meaning: The <radical>stand</radical> radical: a person in a hat standing on the ground. As a kanji, <kanji>stand</kanji>.
立.reading: You stand up to eat a Ritz cracker, りつ. As a verb, たつ is to stand.

手.name: Hand
手.meaning: A wrist with fingers spread: <kanji>hand</kanji>. Squeezed onto the left of other kanji, it becomes the fingers radical.
手.reading: In your hand is a shoe, しゅ, which you're about to throw. 手 on its own is て, and 上手 (skilful) reads じょうず.

力.name: Power
力.meaning: The <radical>power</radical> radical: a flexed arm, all <kanji>power</kanji>.
力.reading: It takes power to launch a rocket, りょく. You'll also see りき, and ちから on its own.

目.name: Eye
目.reading: A mocking bird, もく, stares at you with one huge eye. On its own an eye is め. 目 after a number means "-th": 一つ目, the first.

田.name: Rice Paddy
田.reading: A dentist, でん, wades through the rice paddy to get to work. Surnames use た: 田中, Tanaka.

止.name: Stop
止.meaning: The <radical>stop</radical> radical: a foot planted on the ground. <kanji>Stop</kanji>.
止.reading: A sheep, し, stops dead in the road and won't move. 止まる is to stop.

正.name: Correct
正.meaning: One line on top of <radical>stop</radical>. Stop at the line and you did it <kanji>correct</kanji>ly.
正.reading: The judge sails, せい, past to check. It's also しょう, as in 正月 (New Year). 正しい means correct.

文.name: Writing
文.meaning: The <radical>writing</radical> radical is the kanji itself: <kanji>writing</kanji>. A scholar in a hat, crossing things out as they write.
文.reading: He's writing on a bun, ぶん, because he ran out of paper. 文学 is literature. Also もん, as in 文字 (letter).

口.name: Mouth
口.meaning: The <radical>mouth</radical> radical: <kanji>mouth</kanji>. It also means an opening, like an entrance.
口.reading: A koala, こう, opens its mouth really wide. On its own a mouth is くち; 入口 is an entrance.

町.name: Town
町.meaning: A <radical>rice paddy</radical> next to a <radical>street</radical>. Put a street through the fields and you get a <kanji>town</kanji>.
町.reading: The town sells nothing but chocolate, ちょう. The word on its own is まち.

工.name: Construction
工.meaning: The <radical>craft</radical> radical, an I-beam. As a kanji it means <kanji>construction</kanji>.
工.reading: A koala in a hard hat, こう, runs the construction site. 工場 is a factory.

空.name: Sky
空.meaning: A <radical>roof</radical> on <radical>legs</radical> over a <radical>craft</radical> workshop. Someone knocked the roof off, and now they can see the <kanji>sky</kanji>. It's <kanji>empty</kanji> up there.
空.reading: A cuckoo clock, くう, flies out through the hole. 空港 is an airport; そら on its own is the sky.

足.name: Foot
足.meaning: The <radical>foot</radical> radical is the kanji itself: <kanji>foot</kanji>. A mouth on top of a footprint: a foot that eats everything you step on.
足.reading: The word is あし: your foot has an ash problem from stepping in the campfire. In compounds it's そく, like a sock. 足りる means to be enough.

早.name: Early
早.meaning: The <radical>sun</radical> balanced on a <radical>cross</radical>. When the sun is only as high as a cross, it's still <kanji>early</kanji>.
早.reading: It's early and you yawn "はや..." as in 早い (early). Think ha, yawn. In compounds it's そう.

字.name: Character
字.meaning: A <radical>child</radical> under a <radical>roof</radical>, practising <kanji>character</kanji>s at the kitchen table.
字.reading: The kid is writing in a jeep, じ. 漢字 is kanji; 文字 is a letter.

音.name: Sound
音.meaning: <radical>Stand</radical> in the <radical>sun</radical> on a quiet morning and you hear every <kanji>sound</kanji>.
音.reading: You hear a light switch click on, おん. The everyday word for a sound is おと; 音楽 is music.

花.name: Flower
花.meaning: <radical>Grass</radical> above a <radical>person</radical> holding a <radical>spoon</radical>. They're feeding the grass until it grows into a <kanji>flower</kanji>.
花.reading: Your car, か, is covered in flowers. The word on its own is はな; 花火 (fire flowers) are fireworks.

赤.name: Red
赤.reading: あか: it's so red you say "ah! car!" when you see a fire engine. 赤い is red. In compounds it's せき.

青.name: Blue
青.meaning: The <radical>blue</radical> radical is the kanji itself: <kanji>blue</kanji>. Life growing on the moon, and seen from up there it all looks blue. In Japanese it also covers green, like a green traffic light.
青.reading: You sail, せい, over the blue sea. The word on its own is あお; 青い is blue.

夕.name: Evening
夕.meaning: The <radical>evening</radical> radical: <kanji>evening</kanji>, a crescent moon coming up.
夕.reading: In the evening you play the ukulele, ゆう, under the moon. 夕方 is evening; 夕食 dinner.

犬.name: Dog
犬.meaning: The <radical>dog</radical> radical is the kanji itself: <kanji>dog</kanji>. Something big with a drop by its ear, and the drop is its drool.
犬.reading: It belongs to Ken, けん, your neighbour. The word on its own is いぬ.

会.name: Meet
会.meaning: The <radical>meet</radical> radical is the kanji itself: <kanji>meet</kanji>. A roof with two people and something private under it: they meet in secret.
会.reading: They meet under a kite, かい, so they'll be easy to find. 会社 is a company; 会う is to meet.

同.name: Same
同.meaning: A <radical>helmet</radical> with one line and a <radical>mouth</radical> inside. Everyone in the army wears the <kanji>same</kanji> helmet.
同.reading: They all eat the same donut, どう, for lunch. 同じ means the same.

自.name: Self
自.meaning: The <radical>self</radical> radical: <kanji>self</kanji>. It's a nose, and in Japan you point at your nose to mean yourself.
自.reading: You drive yourself in your own jeep, じ. 自分 is oneself; 自動車 (self-moving car) is a car.

社.name: Company
社.meaning: An <radical>altar</radical> on some <radical>dirt</radical>. That's a shrine, and people who worked at the shrine together formed the first <kanji>company</kanji>.
社.reading: The company boss is a shark, しゃ. 会社 is company; 社会 is society.

地.name: Ground
地.meaning: <radical>Dirt</radical> with a <radical>scorpion</radical> in it. You're down on the <kanji>ground</kanji>, where the scorpions live.
地.reading: A cheetah, ち, sprints across the ground and eats the scorpion. 地図 is a map; 地下鉄 the subway.

方.name: Direction
方.meaning: The <radical>direction</radical> radical: <kanji>direction</kanji>. Politely, it also means a person.
方.reading: Point the hose, ほう, in the right direction. 方 after a verb is "the way to do it": 読み方 (how to read), where it's かた.

新.name: New
新.meaning: <radical>Stand</radical> a <radical>tree</radical> up and take an <radical>axe</radical> to it. You chop fresh wood to build something <kanji>new</kanji>.
新.reading: You chop so hard you hit your shin, しん. 新聞 is a newspaper; 新しい is new.

場.name: Place
場.meaning: <radical>Dirt</radical> that's <radical>easy</radical> to dig. That's the best <kanji>place</kanji> to set up camp.
場.reading: A joker, じょう, pulls it up and moves it. On its own, a place is ば; 場所 is a place and 工場 a factory.

明.name: Bright
明.meaning: The <radical>sun</radical> and the <radical>moon</radical> in the same sky. It's twice as <kanji>bright</kanji>.
明.reading: A maid, めい, has to pull the curtains shut. 明るい is bright; 明日 (tomorrow) is read あした.

京.name: Capital
京.meaning: A <radical>top hat</radical> on a <radical>mouth</radical> above something <radical>small</radical>: a tall tower in the middle of the <kanji>capital</kanji>.
京.reading: It's a Kyoto tower, きょう. Kyoto was the old capital, 京都, and Tokyo, 東京, is the eastern one.

用.name: Use
用.meaning: The <radical>use</radical> radical: <kanji>use</kanji>. It looks like a fence you can use for anything.
用.reading: Use it as a stage for your yo-yo, よう, tricks. 用意 is preparation; 用事 an errand.

通.name: Pass Through
通.meaning: <radical>Mama</radical> riding a <radical>scooter</radical> she likes to <radical>use</radical> every day to <kanji>pass through</kanji> town.
通.reading: One day she rides through a tsunami, つう. 通る is to pass through; 通う to commute.

言.name: Say
言.reading: The genie, げん, says "your wish is my command." 言う is to say; 言葉 is a word.

理.name: Reason
理.meaning: A <radical>king</radical> in the <radical>village</radical>. When he gives an order, he has to give a <kanji>reason</kanji>.
理.reading: His reason is always "because I'm standing on a reef", り. 理由 is a reason; 料理 cooking.

体.name: Body
体.meaning: A <radical>person</radical> next to a <radical>book</radical>. They're reading a book about the human <kanji>body</kanji>.
体.reading: Chapter one is about the tie, たい, which doesn't seem right. 体 on its own is からだ.

作.name: Make
作.meaning: A <radical>person</radical> with a saw-toothed tool beside them, the kind you use to <kanji>make</kanji> things.
作.reading: They make a sack, さく, to carry the tools. 作る is to make; 作文 is an essay.

強.name: Strong
強.meaning: A <radical>bow</radical> next to a <radical>private</radical> <radical>insect</radical>. Only a <kanji>strong</kanji> archer can shoot a bug that small.
強.reading: The archer is from Kyoto, きょう. 勉強 is study; 強い is strong.

公.name: Public
公.meaning: <radical>Eight</radical> over something <radical>private</radical>. When eight people know your secret, it's <kanji>public</kanji>.
公.reading: One of them was a koala, こう, who told everyone. 公園 is a park.

野.name: Field
野.meaning: A <radical>village</radical> planned <radical>in advance</radical> means open <kanji>field</kanji>s all around it.
野.reading: A yak, や, grazes in the field. 野菜 is vegetables; 野球 baseball.

心.name: Heart
心.meaning: The <radical>heart</radical> radical: <kanji>heart</kanji>, and the mind with it.
心.reading: Your heart is in your shin, しん, somehow. 心配 is worry; こころ is heart on its own.

思.name: Think
思.meaning: A <radical>rice paddy</radical> above your <radical>heart</radical>. You <kanji>think</kanji> about the harvest day and night.
思.reading: You think so hard that a sheep, し, has to wake you up. 思う is to think.

家.name: House
家.meaning: A <radical>pig</radical> under a <radical>roof</radical>. In the old days the pig lived in the <kanji>house</kanji> too.
家.reading: A car, か, is parked in the living room as well. It's a strange house. 家族 is family; いえ is house on its own.

多.name: Many
多.meaning: The <radical>many</radical> radical is the kanji itself: <kanji>many</kanji>. Two evenings stacked up. You've been up too many nights.
多.reading: Every night you eat a taco, た. That's a lot of tacos. 多い is many.

教.name: Teach
教.meaning: <radical>Filial piety</radical> and a <radical>whip</radical>. An old-school teacher uses a whip to <kanji>teach</kanji> respect for your elders.
教.reading: The teacher is from Kyoto, きょう. 教室 is a classroom; 教える is to teach.

元.name: Origin
元.meaning: The <radical>origin</radical> radical is the kanji itself: <kanji>origin</kanji>. Two lines on two legs: you started out on two legs, and that's your origin.
元.reading: A genie, げん, knows everyone's origin. 元気 is healthy, energetic.

近.name: Near
近.meaning: An <radical>axe</radical> riding a <radical>scooter</radical>. It's getting <kanji>near</kanji>. Get out of the way.
近.reading: It's the king's axe, きん. 近所 is the neighbourhood; 近い is near.

考.name: Think
考.meaning: An <radical>old man</radical> with his cane bent. He's stopped walking to <kanji>think</kanji> things over. (<kanji>思</kanji> is also think; this one is the slow, careful kind: consider.)
考.reading: He's thinking about a koala, こう. 考える is to think.

画.name: Picture
画.meaning: An <radical>awning</radical> over a <radical>rice paddy</radical> in a <radical>container</radical>. You paint the paddy, frame it, and hang it: it's a <kanji>picture</kanji>.
画.reading: A gaggle of geese, が, poses for the picture. 映画 is a movie. Also かく, for strokes in 画数.

海.name: Sea
海.meaning: <radical>Water</radical> <kanji>every</kanji>where you look, every direction, every day. That's the <kanji>sea</kanji>.
海.reading: Fly a kite, かい, over the sea. 海 on its own is うみ.

売.name: Sell
売.meaning: You already know the <radical>sell</radical> radical, and the kanji means the same: <kanji>sell</kanji>. A samurai with a lid on his head, running around town on two legs trying to sell his armour.
売.reading: He sells it off a bicycle, ばい. 売る is to sell.

知.name: Know
知.meaning: An <radical>arrow</radical> flies into a <radical>mouth</radical>. You <kanji>know</kanji> exactly what to say, straight to the point.
知.reading: A cheetah, ち, knows everything. 知る is to know.

道.name: Road
道.meaning: A <radical>neck</radical> riding a <radical>scooter</radical> down the <kanji>road</kanji>, head held high.
道.reading: It stops for a donut, どう. Martial arts are "ways": 柔道, 剣道. The word on its own is みち.

計.name: Measure
計.meaning: <radical>Say</radical> the <radical>cross</radical>, which is ten. You count out loud to ten to <kanji>measure</kanji> something.
計.reading: You're measuring a cake, けい. 時計 is a clock; 計画 a plan.

朝.name: Morning
朝.meaning: A <radical>cross</radical> stuck in the ground, the <kanji>early</kanji> sun rising behind it, and the <radical>moon</radical> still out. Early sun and a leftover moon: that's <kanji>morning</kanji>.
朝.reading: You have chocolate, ちょう, for breakfast. 朝 on its own is あさ.

台.name: Pedestal
台.meaning: Something <radical>private</radical> over a <radical>mouth</radical>. You put your secret up on a <kanji>pedestal</kanji>.
台.reading: It's a die, だい, on a pedestal. 台 counts machines and cars. 台所 is the kitchen.

広.name: Wide
広.meaning: Something <radical>private</radical> under a <radical>canopy</radical>. The tent is so <kanji>wide</kanji> you can keep all your secrets in it.
広.reading: It's big enough for a koala, こう, to live in. 広い is wide.

少.name: Few
少.meaning: <radical>Small</radical> with a <radical>slide</radical> cutting off the bottom. Something small and getting smaller: only a <kanji>few</kanji> left.
少.reading: Only a few people came to the show, しょう. 少し is a little; 少ない few.

切.name: Cut
切.meaning: <radical>Seven</radical> next to a <radical>sword</radical>. Seven swings of the sword to <kanji>cut</kanji> it.
切.reading: You cut a whole set of dishes, せつ, by accident. 大切 is important; 切る is to cut.

楽.name: Fun
楽.meaning: <radical>White</radical> <radical>ice</radical> on a <radical>tree</radical>. Winter's here and it's <kanji>fun</kanji> in the snow, and there's music.
楽.reading: A goose honks "がく" along, making 音楽 (music). Relaxing is らく, and fun is たのしい.

店.name: Shop
店.meaning: A <radical>fortune</radical> teller under a <radical>canopy</radical>. That's their <kanji>shop</kanji>.
店.reading: They also sell tennis rackets, てん. 店員 is a shop clerk; みせ on its own is a shop.

親.name: Parent
親.meaning: <radical>Stand</radical> in a <radical>tree</radical> to <radical>see</radical> your kid all the way to school. That's a <kanji>parent</kanji>.
親.reading: They fall out and land on their shin, しん. 親切 is kind; おや on its own is a parent.

答.name: Answer
答.meaning: <radical>Bamboo</radical> strips that <radical>fit</radical> together. The pieces fit: that's the <kanji>answer</kanji>.
答.reading: The answer was written by a toad, とう. 答え is an answer; 答える to answer.

夜.name: Night
夜.meaning: A <radical>person</radical> in a <radical>top hat</radical> drags their feet through <radical>winter</radical>, with a <radical>drop</radical> of sweat. They're walking home late at <kanji>night</kanji>.
夜.reading: They're riding a yak, や, home. The word on its own is よる.

帰.name: Return
帰.meaning: A <radical>knife</radical>, a <radical>broom</radical>, a <radical>lid</radical> and a <radical>towel</radical>. You pack the whole kitchen when you <kanji>return</kanji> home.
帰.reading: You lock up with a key, き. 帰る is to go home.

古.name: Old
古.meaning: The <radical>old</radical> radical is the kanji itself: <kanji>old</kanji>. Ten (a cross) over a mouth: something passed down through ten generations of mouths is old.
古.reading: It's an old cobra, こ. 古い is old.

歌.name: Song
歌.meaning: <radical>Can</radical> twice, next to a <radical>yawn</radical>. "Can you, can you..." you open your mouth wide to sing a <kanji>song</kanji>.
歌.reading: You sing it in your car, か. 歌う is to sing; うた is a song.

買.name: Buy
買.meaning: A <radical>net</radical> full of <radical>shell</radical>s. Shells used to be money, and you bring a netful to <kanji>buy</kanji> something.
買.reading: You buy a bicycle, ばい. 買う is to buy; 買い物 shopping.

図.name: Map
図.meaning: A <radical>cross</radical> and some <radical>ice</radical> inside an <radical>enclosure</radical>. X marks the spot on the frozen island: it's a treasure <kanji>map</kanji>.
図.reading: It's a map of the zoo, ず. 地図 is a map; 図書館 a library.

週.name: Week
週.meaning: Riding a <radical>scooter</radical> around one <radical>lap</radical> of the town takes a whole <kanji>week</kanji>.
週.reading: Your shoe, しゅう, wears out every week. 週末 is the weekend; 毎週 every week.

室.name: Room
室.meaning: Under a <radical>roof</radical>, on the <radical>ground</radical>, something <radical>private</radical> over the <radical>dirt</radical>. It's your own private <kanji>room</kanji>.
室.reading: It's full of shirts, しつ. 教室 is a classroom.

歩.name: Walk
歩.meaning: <radical>Stop</radical> every <kanji>few</kanji> steps to look around. Stop, a few steps, stop: you're taking a <kanji>walk</kanji>.
歩.reading: You walk with a garden hose, ほ, dragging behind you. 歩く is to walk; 散歩 a stroll.

風.name: Wind
風.meaning: An <radical>insect</radical> under a <radical>table</radical>, hiding from the <kanji>wind</kanji>.
風.reading: The wind blows a food truck, ふう, over. かぜ on its own is wind; 風呂 is a bath.

紙.name: Paper
紙.meaning: <radical>Thread</radical> and a <radical>clan</radical>. The whole clan beats thread fibres flat to make <kanji>paper</kanji>.
紙.reading: A sheep, し, eats the paper. On its own paper is かみ; 手紙 is a letter.

黒.name: Black
黒.meaning: The <radical>black</radical> radical is the kanji itself: <kanji>black</kanji>. A village over a fire: it burnt down and now everything is black.
黒.reading: Black as a crow: くろ. 黒い is black. In compounds it's こく, as in 黒板 (blackboard).

春.name: Spring
春.meaning: <radical>Spring</radical> over the <radical>sun</radical>. Green shoots and a person strolling in the warm sun: <kanji>spring</kanji>.
春.reading: In spring you finally take off your winter shoes, しゅん. On its own spring is はる.

色.name: Color
色.meaning: The <radical>color</radical> radical is the kanji itself: <kanji>color</kanji>. A hook dangled over a coiled snake, and the snake changes color.
色.reading: It's in shock, しょく. The word on its own is いろ; 景色 is scenery (しき).

走.name: Run
走.meaning: The <radical>run</radical> radical is the kanji itself: <kanji>run</kanji>. Dirt kicked up over a footprint: you run so fast the dirt flies.
走.reading: You run away from a soda can, そう, that just exploded. 走る is to run.

秋.name: Autumn
秋.meaning: <radical>Grain</radical> next to <radical>fire</radical>. The fields turn fire-orange at harvest time: <kanji>autumn</kanji>.
秋.reading: Leaves fill your shoe, しゅう. On its own autumn is あき.

夏.name: Summer
夏.meaning: An <radical>awning</radical> over your <radical>eye</radical>, and legs dragging like it's <radical>winter</radical>. You shade your eyes and drag yourself around in the heat of <kanji>summer</kanji>.
夏.reading: Your car, か, is too hot to touch. On its own summer is なつ.

曜.name: Weekday
曜.meaning: The <radical>sun</radical>, a <radical>broom</radical> and a <radical>turkey</radical>. Each <kanji>weekday</kanji> has a chore on the calendar: sweeping, feeding the turkey...
曜.reading: Every weekday you do yo-yo tricks, よう. All the day names end in 曜日.

肉.name: Meat
肉.reading: The butcher charges a nickel, にく, for it. 牛肉 is beef.

鳥.name: Bird
鳥.reading: The bird is carrying chocolate, ちょう. The word on its own is とり.

冬.name: Winter
冬.meaning: <radical>Winter</radical> drags its feet over <radical>two</radical> little patches of ice. It's <kanji>winter</kanji>.
冬.reading: Your toes freeze, and so does a toad, とう. On its own winter is ふゆ.

昼.name: Noon
昼.meaning: A <radical>measure</radical> held up to the <radical>sun</radical> on the <radical>ground</radical>. The shadow is shortest: it's <kanji>noon</kanji>.
昼.reading: Time to give the dog its chew toy, ちゅう. On its own it's ひる; 昼ご飯 is lunch.

茶.name: Tea
茶.meaning: <radical>Grass</radical> over a <radical>person</radical> sitting under a <radical>tree</radical>. They pick leaves from the bush and brew <kanji>tea</kanji> in the shade.
茶.reading: The word is <reading>ちゃ</reading>, which is where "chai" comes from. <ja>お茶</ja> is tea; <ja>喫茶店</ja> a café (<ja>さ</ja>).

弟.name: Younger Brother
弟.meaning: <radical>Eight</radical> arrows, a <radical>bow</radical>, a <radical>stick</radical> and a <radical>slide</radical>. Your <kanji>younger brother</kanji> made a toy bow from a stick and fires all eight arrows at you from the top of the slide.
弟.reading: He's hiding under the table, てい. On its own it's おとうと.

牛.name: Cow
牛.meaning: The <radical>cow</radical> radical: <kanji>cow</kanji>. <kanji>午</kanji> (noon) with a horn poking up.
牛.reading: Cows make everything gooey, ぎゅう. 牛乳 is milk; 牛肉 beef.

魚.name: Fish
魚.meaning: The <radical>fish</radical> radical is the kanji itself: <kanji>fish</kanji>. A hook over a rice paddy over the fire: catch it in the paddy and grill it.
魚.reading: Serve it with a gyoza, ぎょ. On its own a fish is さかな.

兄.name: Older Brother
兄.meaning: A big <radical>mouth</radical> on <radical>legs</radical>. That's your <kanji>older brother</kanji>, telling you what to do.
兄.reading: He's eating all the cake, けい. On its own it's あに, or おにいさん.
